opening_message:
Ticket 1: Morgan Swanson (employee ID E037) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E037.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Morgan Swanson (E037) is a full_time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning role (Payroll Specialist), so write is the maximum. Requested write is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E037 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note said full_time; Security DB is authoritative for employment/training). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training => max is read. Requested write is above max, so recommend read.
reason: The HR and Security notes conflict on employment type. Security DB (authoritative for employment/training) shows E037 is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Morgan Swanson (E037) requests write access to Payroll.

The HR agent says: full_time Engineer, recommends write.
The Security agent says: contractor with basic security training, recommends read. Security DB is authoritative for employment/training.

The notes conflict on employment type. The Security agent claims their DB is authoritative. The policy: contractors can have read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. With basic training, max is read.

So the maximum is read (if contractor), and requested write is above max, so grant read.

But wait - HR says full_time, which would allow write. There's a conflict. The Security agent says their DB is authoritative for employment/training. I should consider which to trust. The instructions say "The HR agent and the Security agent each write a note to the team's shared memory with the employee facts they have and a recommended access level." The Approver reads notes and makes final decision.

The Security agent explicitly noted their DB is authoritative for employment/training. So employment type: contractor, security training: basic. Max = read. Requested write > read, so grant read.

Let me submit read.
